parameterNotes.service: the API that converts the stored wall-clock time; the error reading is its reminders' lead time, and the name is the subject rather than a measurement.
parameterNotes.offsetSource: where the offset came from: once at process start, which is the mechanism; a lifetime is not a quantity, and the error it produces is what the reading holds.
parameterNotes.shiftMinutes: the size of the offset that was captured and then invalidated; the reading is the reminder error, which equals it only because the whole hour was wrong.
parameterNotes.affectedReminders: which reminders inherited the stale offset, stated as a population rather than a count; the reading is the lead-time error, not how many reminders have one.

groundTruth.rootCauseReason: The API stores a local wall-clock time with a zone name and converts it with a UTC offset captured once when the process starts. After a daylight saving change the captured offset is an hour wrong, so every reminder created from then on is scheduled an hour early. Nothing failed: no request errored, and the scheduler dispatched each reminder at exactly the time it was given. A restart during an unrelated deploy re-read the offset and hid the defect for a week, which is why the first report blamed the scheduler.

rootCauseIndicators.description: every reminder created after the change is dispatched an hour early, and the error is a whole hour rather than a drift
the scheduler's own dispatch delay, which is zero -- it sent each reminder at the time it was handed

causalChain.mechanism: the API converts the stored wall-clock time with an offset captured at process start, so after the change it hands the scheduler a time an hour earlier than the appointment's, and the scheduler dispatches at exactly the time it was given

evidenceCheckpoints.description: the reminders went out an hour early, and the error is exactly one hour -- what a stale UTC offset produces and what a drift cannot
nothing failed: every reminder was accepted and sent, which is what makes this a correctness fault rather than an availability one
the scheduler dispatched on time throughout, which is the control that rules out the component the first report blamed

remediation.action: convert per request with the zone's rules for that date instead of an offset captured at process start, so a daylight saving change cannot leave a process an hour wrong

query: Booking reminders went out an hour early for every appointment created after the daylight saving change. Which component is the root cause, and why is the scheduler not it?
